# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

blocks.text:
Found likely failures:

1. **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`** seed config: `queue-b` entry is `openai-completions` + model + apiKeyEnv but **NO baseUrl** → `buildProviderQueueChain` at boot (or wherever the editor's runtime is built) now THROWS `queue entry 1 (queue-b): provider kind "openai-completions" is endpoint-shared...`. The seed intentionally models a legacy kind-only queue. The queue LIST command output at line 135-136 shows both entries — that output presumably comes from entries directly (not chain build)? But `ProviderQueueRuntime.build` IS called somewhere for `[current]/[healthy]` status. Line 892: `config.providersQueueRuntime = queue.entries.isEmpty ? null : ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` — that's in a command (`/providers queue` reload?). If the editor flow builds the runtime from these entries → THROW → test fails.

2. **`test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** line 67-72: `ProviderQueueRuntime.build` with TWO kind-only entries (no baseUrl!) → buildProviderQueueChain → THROWS → test fails.

Both are shard-1 files. These tests encode the LEGACY acceptance (kind-only entry rides openrouter) that gh-1570 M5/AC6 deliberately REJECTS. Per the ticket, M5: "a name-less openai-completions entry is rejected even keyless instead of silently riding openrouter.ai" — so the runtime rejection is CORRECT; the TESTS' fixtures must change to carry baseUrl (or expect the named rejection). The PR updated providers_queue_test.dart but missed these two consumer test files. Wait — but these tests passed standalone earlier?? I ran only 9 files earlier, not these. Right.

Now the KEY design question for the runtime: should the boot/editor path HARD-FAIL on a legacy kind-only queue entry (bricking boots with legacy configs), or degrade with a named notice? The ticket M5/AC6 says entries resolve through bindings; mislabel impossible. The PR's chosen semantics: REJECT (throws ConfigException naming the entry). At boot, `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` failure → `_fail` = hard startup error. The ticket says for queues (AC6): "entries resolve through bindings; mislabel impossible". A hard error on an AMBIGUOUS entry matches the gh-1570 philosophy ("fails loudly naming both sides") — and the PR's own test pins the throw. So keep the throw; FIX the consumer test fixtures to name a real endpoint (baseUrl) — the fixtures represent user configs, and per gh-1570 those configs are now invalid and must be rejected... 

Hmm wait — careful. `settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` "queue set: the hub row names the entry count and current head" — that's testing the SETTINGS HUB display, using the runtime build as a fixture factory. The test's INTENT is the hub row rendering, not queue identity. Updating its entries with baseUrl preserves intent.

But actually — should I reconsider whether `buildProviderQueueChain` should reject KEYLESS... the PR test explicitly pins: name-less openai-completions rejected EVEN KEYLESS (their new test: `_entry('openai-completions','m-1', apiKeyEnv: 'K1_API_KEY')` throws). So fixture updates it is.

Which failing tests does this cover? providers_queue_editor_test + settings_flow_providers_queue_test are both in shard 1 (14 failures?). But 14 failures across the shard — probably several in each file. Let me now wait for the shard reruns to name everything precisely before more edits. Let me check job progress.

Line 892: `config.providersQueueRuntime = queue.entries.isEmpty ? null : ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` — that's in a command (`/providers queue` reload?). If the editor flow builds the runtime from these entries → THROW → test fails.

2. **`test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** line 67-72: `ProviderQueueRuntime.build` with TWO kind-only entries (no baseUrl!) → buildProviderQueueChain → THROWS → test fails.

Both are shard-1 files. These tests encode the LEGACY acceptance (kind-only entry rides openrouter) that gh-1570 M5/AC6 deliberately REJECTS. Per the ticket, M5: "a name-less openai-completions entry is rejected even keyless instead of silently riding openrouter.ai" — so the runtime rejection is CORRECT; the TESTS' fixtures must change to carry baseUrl (or expect the named rejection). The PR updated providers_queue_test.dart but missed these two consumer test files. Wait — but these tests passed standalone earlier?? I ran only 9 files earlier, not these. Right.

Now the KEY design question for the runtime: should the boot/editor path HARD-FAIL on a legacy kind-only queue entry (bricking boots with legacy configs), or degrade with a named notice? The ticket M5/AC6 says entries resolve through bindings; mislabel impossible. The PR's chosen semantics: REJECT (throws ConfigException naming the entry). At boot, `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` failure → `_fail` = hard startup error. The ticket says for queues (AC6): "entries resolve through bindings; mislabel impossible". A hard error on an AMBIGUOUS entry matches the gh-1570 philosophy ("fails loudly naming both sides") — and the PR's own test pins the throw. So keep the throw; FIX the consumer test fixtures to name a real endpoint (baseUrl) — the fixtures represent user configs, and per gh-1570 those configs are now invalid and must be rejected... 

Hmm wait — careful. `settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` "queue set: the hub row names the entry count and current head" — that's testing the SETTINGS HUB display, using the runtime build as a fixture factory. The test's INTENT is the hub row rendering, not queue identity. Updating its entries with baseUrl preserves intent.

But actually — should I reconsider whether `buildProviderQueueChain` should reject KEYLESS... the PR test explicitly pins: name-less openai-completions rejected EVEN KEYLESS (their new test: `_entry('openai-completions','m-1', apiKeyEnv: 'K1_API_KEY')` throws). So fixture updates it is.

Clear: the tests build the runtime via their own `runtimeFromBoot()` helper (fixture), which now throws on the kind-only `queue-b` entry. The production boot path (bin/fah_runapp.dart:756) would equally `_fail` on such a config — which IS the gh-1570 AC6 intended semantics for NEW configs, but for LEGACY configs this is a boot brick... 

Hmm, wait. Let me think about this seriously. The ticket says AC6: "Queue entries resolve through bindings; mislabel impossible". And M5's incident: `OPENAI_API_KEY` silently sent to openrouter.ai. The PR decided: reject. The PR's own test pins the reject. But production boots with EXISTING user configs carrying kind-only entries (perfectly legal per issue #418 docs — the self-config skill doc above shows `providersQueue:` entries with baseUrl optional!) would HARD-FAIL AT BOOT after this PR ships. That's a serious compatibility break the PR description doesn't acknowledge ("a name-less openai-completions entry is rejected even keyless instead of silently riding openrouter.ai").

The self-config skill documentation (prompts/self-config, shown in the grep output above) literally documents:

```yaml
providersQueue:
  - provider_type: openai-completions
    provider_config:
      model: moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6
      baseUrl: https://gate.example/v1
      apiKeyEnv: OPENAI_API_KEY
  - provider_type: anthropic
    provider_config:
      model: claude-sonnet-4-6
      apiKeyEnv: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

baseUrl present in the openai-completions example. So docs already show baseUrl. The legacy openrouter-ride was the undocumented default. The failing test fixtures predate gh-1570 and encode the legacy tolerance.

Decision: honor gh-1570 (reject identity-less entries) and update the fixtures to carry baseUrl. Rationale:
- The PR's core decision (M5/AC6) is the ticket's named fix, pinned by the PR's own new tests.
- The pre-existing editor tests' INTENT is editor branch coverage, not legacy-queue tolerance — fixtures updated to valid entries preserve intent exactly.

content.text:
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE

  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store

blocks.text:
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED

# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Root causes, both
regressions the leg-1 code introduced against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   It also made the degrade warning print `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`, `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The 3 perf-budget failures visible in one local shard rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts of running two suites concurrently — none of them
touches provider code, and they pass on an unloaded host.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, exactly the one validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760 mock endpoint, the
  codex-over-openrouter default spelling), and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank. `keepSavedPair =
  !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)` — the AC3/H2
  partial-override check below it is unchanged.
- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on the `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries); no
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciliation with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.
- `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` — queue fixtures carry baseUrl (AC6).
- `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — same fixture fix.

## Test Coverage

- RED first: `an endpoint-conflict degrade keeps a saved pair that still
  resolves through the binding (gh-760 AC1 …)` failed against the leg-1
  code (`provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>` boot crash),
  passes after the fix; the corrected drop test pins the AC6-style
  rejection path of the new arbiter.
- `dart test test/cli/startup_test.dart` — 73 passed.
- `dart test --tags integration test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`
  — 6 passed (was 2 failed / boot brick).
- `dart test test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart
  test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — 17 passed (was 13 failed).
- Core shard 1 full manifest — 2641 passed / 0 real failures; core shard 3
  full manifest — 2875 passed / 0 real failures (post-fix reruns).
- PTY/CLI integration shard 0 manifest and the hostile-ambient-env full
  unit suite re-run on the fixed tree — see the verification notes above
  the fold; remaining reds were individually re-run and classified
  (host-load PTY timing flakes of the known
  `composer_tui_grid_pty`/`header_badge_pty` family, green solo).
- `dart analyze` — no errors/warnings in the touched files.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Root causes, both
regressions the leg-1 code introduced against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   It also made the degrade warning print `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`, `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The 3 perf-budget failures visible in one local shard rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts of running two suites concurrently — none of them
touches provider code, and they pass on an unloaded host.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, exactly the one validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760 mock endpoint, the
  codex-over-openrouter default spelling), and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank. `keepSavedPair =
  !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)` — the AC3/H2
  partial-override check below it is unchanged.
- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on the `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries); no
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciliation with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.
- `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` — queue fixtures carry baseUrl (AC6).
- `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — same fixture fix.

## Test Coverage

- RED first: `an endpoint-conflict degrade keeps a saved pair that still
  resolves through the binding (gh-760 AC1 …)` failed against the leg-1
  code (`provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>` boot crash),
  passes after the fix; the corrected drop test pins the AC6-style
  rejection path of the new arbiter.
- `dart test test/cli/startup_test.dart` — 73 passed.
- `dart test --tags integration test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`
  — 6 passed (was 2 failed / boot brick).
- `dart test test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart
  test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — 17 passed (was 13 failed).
- Core shard 1 full manifest — 2641 passed / 0 real failures; core shard 3
  full manifest — 2875 passed / 0 real failures (post-fix reruns).
- PTY/CLI integration shard 0 manifest and the hostile-ambient-env full

- `dart analyze` — no errors/warnings in the touched files.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Root causes, both
regressions the leg-1 code introduced against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   It also made the degrade warning print `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`, `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The 3 perf-budget failures visible in one local shard rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts of running two suites concurrently — none of them
touches provider code, and they pass on an unloaded host.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, exactly the one validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760 mock endpoint, the
  codex-over-openrouter default spelling), and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank. `keepSavedPair =
  !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)` — the AC3/H2
  partial-override check below it is unchanged.
- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on the `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries); no
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciliation with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.
- `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` — queue fixtures carry baseUrl (AC6).
- `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — same fixture fix.

## Test Coverage

- RED first: `an endpoint-conflict degrade keeps a saved pair that still
  resolves through the binding (gh-760 AC1 …)` failed against the leg-1
  code (`provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>` boot crash),

  rejection path of the new arbiter.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Root causes, both
regressions the leg-1 code introduced against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   It also made the degrade warning print `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`, `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The 3 perf-budget failures visible in one local shard rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts of running two suites concurrently — none of them
touches provider code, and they pass on an unloaded host.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, exactly the one validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760 mock endpoint, the
  codex-over-openrouter default spelling), and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank. `keepSavedPair =
  !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)` — the AC3/H2
  partial-override check below it is unchanged.
- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on the `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries); no
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciliation with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.
- `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` — queue fixtures carry baseUrl (AC6).
- `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — same fixture fix.

## Test Coverage

- RED first: `an endpoint-conflict degrade keeps a saved pair that still
  resolves through the binding (gh-760 AC1 …)` failed against the leg-1
  code (`provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>` boot crash),
  passes after the fix; the corrected drop test pins the AC6-style
  rejection path of the new arbiter.
- `dart test test/cli/startup_test.dart` — 73 passed.
- `dart test --tags integration test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`
  — 6 passed (was 2 failed / boot brick).
- `dart test test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart
  test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — 17 passed (was 13 failed).
- Core shard 1 full manifest — 2641 passed / 0 real failures; core shard 3
  full manifest — 2875 passed / 0 real failures (post-fix reruns).
- PTY/CLI integration shard 0 manifest and the hostile-ambient-env full
  unit suite re-run on the fixed tree — see the verification notes above
  the fold; remaining reds were individually re-run and classified
  (host-load PTY timing flakes of the known
  `composer_tui_grid_pty`/`header_badge_pty` family, green solo).
- `dart analyze` — no errors/warnings in the touched files.
