{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciled with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.

blocks.text:
## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciled with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.
- `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` — queue fixtures carry `baseUrl` (AC6).
- `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — same fixture fix.

## Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN for the boot brick: `an endpoint-conflict degrade keeps a saved
  pair that still resolves through the binding (gh-760 AC1 …)` failed
  against the leg-1 code and passes after the fix; the corrected drop test
  pins the arbiter's rejection path.
- `dart test test/cli/startup_test.dart` — 73 passed.
- `dart test --tags integration test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`

  test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — 17 passed (was 13 failed).
- Core shard 1 full manifest — 2641 passed, 0 real failures; core shard 3

- PTY/CLI integration shard 0 manifest (CI selection) — the gh-760 and
  queue suites green in-shard; only the two known host-load PTY timing
  flakes red, both green solo/quarantined (see Issues/Notes).
- Hostile ambient env (CI's exact env: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai` +
  `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` + `FAH_PROVIDER` + `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`), full unit
  suite — **10544 passed, 0 failed**.
- `dart analyze` — 0 errors / 0 warnings; `dart format` clean on all

+# merge guard (sm_merge_guard.py), gh-1568.
+#
+# Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no real runs):
+#   AC1 (the gh-1568 regression) a merge-commit landing whose tree equals

+#   AC4 the race: a validation still in_progress at push time can never

+#       in_progress-at-push means the merge beat the validation).
+#   AC5 a failed tree lookup (commit API 404) degrades to a warning and
+#       alarms — never a false validate, never a traceback.
+#   AC6 the alarm body renders each considered run's resolved tree, so
+#       future alarms are self-diagnosing, and files with the
+#       bug+sm-guard labels (dedup convention untouched).

+GUARD="$HERE/sm_merge_guard.py"
+TMP="$(mktemp -d)"

+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}
+check_absent() { # check_absent <desc> <grep-exit-code: 1 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" != "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}

+# (same as test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart's Process.run('python3')).

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1537 AC5 SM
+# merge guard (sm_merge_guard.py), gh-1568.
+#
+# Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no real runs):
+#   AC1 (the gh-1568 regression) a merge-commit landing whose tree equals
+#       a successful dispatch's commit tree VALIDATES — with the commits
+#       API served in its REAL shape (tree nested under `commit`, no
+#       top-level `tree` key). The shipped `.tree.sha` jq path resolved
+#       empty for every run, so every merge-commit landing false-alarmed
+#       (issue #1568: merges 392fe540ae of #1484 and afed64bfd0 of #1468
+#       both carried trees byte-identical to their green validations).
+#   AC2 an UNCOVERED tree still alarms (exit 3) — the fix must not mute
+#       the invariant.
+#   AC3 a fast-forward landing (pushed sha == validated head sha)
+#       validates with no tree lookup at all.
+#   AC4 the race: a validation still in_progress at push time can never
+#       certify — alarm (the SM merges strictly after green, so
+#       in_progress-at-push means the merge beat the validation).
+#   AC5 a failed tree lookup (commit API 404) degrades to a warning and
+#       alarms — never a false validate, never a traceback.
+#   AC6 the alarm body renders each considered run's resolved tree, so
+#       future alarms are self-diagnosing, and files with the
+#       bug+sm-guard labels (dedup convention untouched).
+# Same discipline as check_lockfiles_selftest.sh (#1100 pattern).

+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+GUARD="$HERE/sm_merge_guard.py"
+TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap '[ "${KEEP:-0}" = 1 ] || rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
+
+fails=0
+check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}
+check_absent() { # check_absent <desc> <grep-exit-code: 1 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" != "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}
+# Via the interpreter, not the shebang: checkouts may drop the exec bit
+# (same as test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart's Process.run('python3')).

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

  ProviderModelBinding.resolve(providerKind: provider, modelId: parsed.model!, baseUrl: keepSavedPair ? baseUrl : (parsed.baseUrl ?? degradedDefault), provenance: flag);

The EFFECTIVE binding: provider = resolved provider (preconfig kind wins over saved), model = parsed.model ?? preconfig model (but only when flag present do we revalidate... careful: if ONLY --base-url is given, the model comes from preconfig (already validated against the PRECONFIG's endpoint), but the endpoint changed → must revalidate model+newEndpoint. - provider = preconfig.spec.kind (via _bootProvider)
- baseUrl = parsed.baseUrl ?? preconfig.baseUrl
- modelId = parsed.model ?? preconfig.modelId

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciled with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.
- `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` — queue fixtures carry `baseUrl` (AC6).
- `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — same fixture fix.

## Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN for the boot brick: `an endpoint-conflict degrade keeps a saved
  pair that still resolves through the binding (gh-760 AC1 …)` failed
  against the leg-1 code and passes after the fix; the corrected drop test
  pins the arbiter's rejection path.
- `dart test test/cli/startup_test.dart` — 73 passed.
- `dart test --tags integration test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`
  — 6 passed (was 2 failed with the boot crash).
- `dart test test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart
  test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — 17 passed (was 13 failed).
- Core shard 1 full manifest — 2641 passed, 0 real failures; core shard 3
  full manifest — 2875 passed, 0 failed (post-fix reruns; perf items solo-green).
- PTY/CLI integration shard 0 manifest (CI selection) — the gh-760 and
  queue suites green in-shard; only the two known host-load PTY timing
  flakes red, both green solo/quarantined (see Issues/Notes).
- Hostile ambient env (CI's exact env: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai` +
  `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` + `FAH_PROVIDER` + `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`), full unit
  suite — **10544 passed, 0 failed**.
- `dart analyze` — 0 errors / 0 warnings; `dart format` clean on all

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1537 AC5 SM
+# merge guard (sm_merge_guard.py), gh-1568.
+#
+# Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no real runs):
+#   AC1 (the gh-1568 regression) a merge-commit landing whose tree equals
+#       a successful dispatch's commit tree VALIDATES — with the commits
+#       API served in its REAL shape (tree nested under `commit`, no
+#       top-level `tree` key). The shipped `.tree.sha` jq path resolved
+#       empty for every run, so every merge-commit landing false-alarmed
+#       (issue #1568: merges 392fe540ae of #1484 and afed64bfd0 of #1468
+#       both carried trees byte-identical to their green validations).
+#   AC2 an UNCOVERED tree still alarms (exit 3) — the fix must not mute
+#       the invariant.
+#   AC3 a fast-forward landing (pushed sha == validated head sha)
+#       validates with no tree lookup at all.
+#   AC4 the race: a validation still in_progress at push time can never
+#       certify — alarm (the SM merges strictly after green, so
+#       in_progress-at-push means the merge beat the validation).
+#   AC5 a failed tree lookup (commit API 404) degrades to a warning and
+#       alarms — never a false validate, never a traceback.
+#   AC6 the alarm body renders each considered run's resolved tree, so
+#       future alarms are self-diagnosing, and files with the
+#       bug+sm-guard labels (dedup convention untouched).
+# Same discipline as check_lockfiles_selftest.sh (#1100 pattern).
+set -u
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+GUARD="$HERE/sm_merge_guard.py"
+TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap '[ "${KEEP:-0}" = 1 ] || rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
+
+fails=0
+check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}
+check_absent() { # check_absent <desc> <grep-exit-code: 1 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" != "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}
+# Via the interpreter, not the shebang: checkouts may drop the exec bit
+# (same as test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart's Process.run('python3')).
+run_guard() { python3 "$GUARD" "$@"; }
+
+# The real shas from the #1568 false alarm (merge of #1484):
+PUSHED_SHA=392fe540ae739931bdc348b607f3a02533b9dd9b

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciled with gh-760).

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test

   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are

  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {

        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
